title: Estimation, Costing & Valuation: Numerical Practice Set 1 (Moderate to Hard)
instructions: All 40 questions are numerical, of moderate to hard level. Keep rough paper ready.
Use the factors given in each question (dry volume factor, volume of a cement bag, and so on).

questions.question: A brick wall is 4 m long, 3 m high and 20 cm thick, with one door opening of 1 m × 2 m. Using modular bricks of nominal size 20 cm × 10 cm × 10 cm (including mortar), the number of bricks required is:
A single room has internal dimensions 4 m × 3 m and walls 30 cm thick. The total centre-line length of the walls is:
questions.explanation: Centre-to-centre dimensions are 4.3 m and 3.3 m. Total length = 2 × (4.3 + 3.3) = 15.2 m.

questions.question: A single room has internal dimensions 5 m × 4 m, with walls 20 cm thick and 3 m high. Ignoring openings, the volume of brickwork in the walls is:

The total centre-line length of the walls of a building is 40 m and there are two T-junctions. The foundation trench is 0.9 m wide and 1 m deep. By the centre-line method, the volume of earthwork in excavation is:
questions.explanation: Deduct half the trench width for each T-junction: length = 40 − 2 × (0.9 / 2) = 39.1 m. Volume = 39.1 × 0.9 × 1 = 35.19 m³.

questions.question: A room 5 m × 4 m internally is 3 m high. It has one door of 1 m × 2 m and two windows of 1.5 m × 1.2 m each. If the full area of all openings is deducted, the area of internal wall plaster is:
questions.explanation: Wall area = 2 × (5 + 4) × 3 = 54 m². Openings = 2 + 2 × 1.8 = 5.6 m². Plaster area = 54 − 5.6 = 48.4 m².

questions.question: Concrete of mix 1:2:4 is needed for 10 m³ of finished work. Take the dry volume as 1.54 times the wet volume and one bag of cement as 0.035 m³. The number of cement bags required is approximately:
Concrete of mix 1:1.5:3 is needed for 5 m³ of finished work. Taking the dry volume as 1.54 times the wet volume, the volume of sand required is:
Using the formula weight per metre = d²/162 kg (d in mm), the weight of a 16 mm diameter steel bar 12 m long is approximately:
questions.explanation: Weight per metre = 16² / 162 = 1.58 kg. For 12 m: 1.58 × 12 ≈ 18.96 kg.

questions.question: An RCC slab measures 5 m × 4 m × 120 mm. For a preliminary estimate, steel is taken as 1% of the concrete volume. If the density of steel is 7850 kg/m³, the weight of steel is:
A room of 6 m × 4.5 m is to be floored with 30 cm × 30 cm tiles. Allowing 5% extra for wastage, the number of tiles required is:

A road embankment has a formation width of 10 m and side slopes of 2:1 (horizontal : vertical). The heights at two sections 100 m apart are 2 m and 3 m. By the mid-sectional area method, the volume of earthwork is:
questions.explanation: Mean height = 2.5 m. Mid-section area = (b + sd)d = (10 + 2 × 2.5) × 2.5 = 37.5 m². Volume = 37.5 × 100 = 3750 m³.

questions.question: A cutting has a formation width of 8 m and side slopes of 1.5:1. The depths at two sections 50 m apart are 1 m and 3 m. By the mean sectional area method, the volume of earthwork is:
The cross-sectional areas of an embankment at the two ends and at the middle of a 60 m length are 20 m², 44 m² and 30 m² respectively. By the prismoidal formula, the volume is:
The cross-sectional areas of a cutting at 20 m intervals are 10, 14, 18, 16 and 12 m². By the trapezoidal (average end area) rule, the volume of earthwork is:
The cross-sectional areas of a cutting at 20 m intervals are 10, 14, 18, 16 and 12 m². By the prismoidal (Simpson's) rule, the volume of earthwork is approximately:
A pipe trench is 1.2 m wide, 1.5 m deep and 200 m long. A pipe of 0.6 m external diameter is laid in it. Ignoring bulking, the volume of earth needed to refill the trench is approximately:
Offsets measured at 10 m intervals from a chain line to a curved boundary are 0, 2.5, 3.5, 4.0, 3.0, 2.0 and 0 m. By Simpson's rule, the area between the chain line and the boundary is approximately:
A circular well has an internal diameter of 3 m and brick steining 30 cm thick, for a depth of 10 m. The volume of brickwork in the steining is approximately:
Sand is stacked in a conical heap with a base diameter of 4 m and a height of 1.5 m. The volume of sand is approximately:

A road 1 km long and 3.75 m wide is to get a metalled layer of 75 mm compacted thickness. Loose metal must be spread 100 mm thick to give 75 mm after compaction. The volume of loose metal required is:
questions.explanation: Loose volume = 1000 × 3.75 × 0.100 = 375 m³. (The compacted volume is 281.25 m³.)

questions.question: Brickwork needs 0.25 m³ of wet mortar per m³. Take the dry volume of mortar as 1.33 times the wet volume and one bag of cement as 0.035 m³. For 10 m³ of brickwork in 1:6 cement mortar, the number of cement bags required is approximately:

100 m² of wall is to be plastered 12 mm thick in 1:4 cement mortar. Add 20% to the wet volume for filling joints and unevenness, take the dry volume as 1.33 times the wet volume, and one bag of cement as 0.035 m³. The number of cement bags required is approximately:
For 1 m³ of 1:2:4 concrete, take the dry volume as 1.52 times the wet volume and the density of cement as 1440 kg/m³. The weight of cement required is approximately:

For one cubic metre of an item, materials cost ₹4000 and labour costs ₹1500. Water charges at 1.5% and contractor's profit at 10% are both added on the cost of materials and labour. The rate per cubic metre is:
One mason can lay 1.25 m³ of brickwork in a day. The number of masons needed to complete 50 m³ of brickwork in 8 days is:
A surface of 300 m² is to be given two coats of paint. If one litre covers 15 m² per coat, the paint required is:
questions.explanation: Total coverage needed = 300 × 2 = 600 m². Paint = 600 / 15 = 40 litres.

questions.question: A truck of 6 m³ capacity is hired at ₹800 per hour. Each round trip, including loading and unloading, takes 2 hours. The cost of carting one cubic metre of material is approximately:
questions.explanation: Cost per trip = 800 × 2 = ₹1600 for 6 m³. Cost per m³ = 1600 / 6 ≈ ₹266.67.

questions.question: One cubic metre of brickwork needs 500 bricks at ₹8000 per thousand and 0.3 m³ of mortar at ₹4000 per m³. Labour costs ₹1200 per m³. The cost of one cubic metre of brickwork is:

A building has a plinth area of 150 m² and the plinth area rate is ₹18,000 per m². Services at 8% and contingencies at 5% are both added on the cost of the building. The approximate total estimate is:
A building is 12 m × 10 m in plan and 3.5 m high. By the cubical content method at ₹4500 per m³, its approximate cost is:
A building costs ₹5,00,000 and has a scrap value of ₹50,000 at the end of its 30-year life. By the straight-line method, its book value after 10 years is:
A machine costs ₹1,00,000 and its scrap value after 5 years is ₹10,000. By the constant percentage (declining balance) method, the annual rate of depreciation is approximately:
A sinking fund is to accumulate ₹1,00,000 in 20 years at 5% compound interest. The annual instalment is approximately:
For a property yielding a net income in perpetuity, the year's purchase at 8% interest is:
A property has a future life of 20 years. Interest on capital is 8% and the sinking fund earns 5%. The year's purchase is approximately:
A property gives a net annual income of ₹60,000 in perpetuity. At 6% interest, its capitalised value is:
questions.explanation: Capitalised value = net income × YP = 60,000 × (100 / 6) = ₹10,00,000 = 10 lakh.

questions.question: A building fetches a gross rent of ₹20,000 per month. Outgoings are 25% of the gross rent. At 8% interest in perpetuity, the capitalised value of the property is:

Land costs ₹5 lakh and the building on it costs ₹15 lakh. The owner expects a net return of 6% on the land and 8% on the building. If outgoings are 30% of the gross rent, the monthly gross rent should be approximately:
An asset costs ₹2,00,000 and depreciates at 10% per year by the declining balance method. Its book value after 3 years is:
A building would cost ₹20 lakh to construct new. Its total life is 60 years, its age is 20 years and its scrap value is 10% of the cost. By straight-line depreciation, its present value is:
questions.explanation: Depreciable amount = 20 − 2 = 18 lakh. Depreciation for 20 years = 18 × 20 / 60 = 6 lakh. Present value = 20 − 6 = 14 lakh.
